skill.name: gh-address-comments

skill.summary: Find and address GitHub PR review comments with gh CLI guidance.

security_audit.summary: The skill contains legitimate GitHub PR review workflow guidance, but it also asks agents to use elevated network and sandbox permissions. The hidden PostToolUse logging hook is a confirmed filesystem risk because it writes to a hidden home-directory file without explicit user action.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the PostToolUse hook or write only to a visible project-local log after explicit user opt-in.
Remove broad elevated network and sandbox guidance. Request the minimum GitHub CLI access needed for each step.
Avoid recommending workflow scope unless required. Document the minimum GitHub scopes needed for comment reading and replies.

finding_verdicts.reason: The text directs agents to run gh commands with elevated network access, which enables external repository operations. The command name is fixed, but the elevated network instruction creates real operational risk.
The instruction asks for escalated sandbox permissions and workflow/repo scopes for gh auth status. That can encourage broad token grants and bypass normal sandbox controls.
The text only tells the user to run gh auth login if authentication or rate limits fail. It is a fixed, user-mediated recovery command with no credential capture or dynamic command construction.
The command substitution is only $(date) inside a fixed logging command. It does not include user input or dynamic command construction, so command injection is not evident.
The PostToolUse hook appends to ~/.claude/gh-address-comments.log in a hidden home directory after Bash use. Persistent hidden logging is a real filesystem side effect that users may not expect.
The same hook writes to a hidden path in the user's home directory. Even though the message is generic, background hidden writes create privacy and auditability risk.

content.value_statement: Review comments can be hard to track across a busy pull request. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through finding comments, choosing fixes, and applying changes with GitHub CLI.
actual_capabilities: Guides use of gh CLI to find the open pull request for the current branch.
Checks GitHub CLI authentication before running PR comment tasks.
Directs the assistant to summarize review threads and ask which comments to address.
Helps apply fixes only for comments selected by the user.
Includes retry guidance for GitHub authentication or rate limit problems.
limitations: Requires the GitHub CLI to be installed and authenticated.
Needs network access and repository permissions for the target pull request.
The referenced fetch_comments.py helper is not included in the packaged file structure.
Does not decide which comments to fix without user selection.

use_cases.title: Solo Developer Cleanup
use_cases.description: Review a current branch PR, list actionable comments, and fix only the items the developer selects.

use_cases.title: Maintainer Review Triage
use_cases.description: Summarize unresolved review threads before deciding which feedback should become code changes.

use_cases.title: Team PR Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Coordinate selected fixes after a review cycle while keeping GitHub authentication checks explicit.

prompt_templates.title: List Review Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-address-comments to inspect the open PR for my current branch. Summarize each review thread and wait for my selection.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Selected Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-address-comments on this branch. Number the PR comments, ask which ones to fix, then apply changes for my selected items.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Before Editing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-address-comments to separate blocking comments from suggestions. Ask me which blocking items to address before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Recover Auth Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-address-comments for this PR. If GitHub authentication or rate limits fail, pause and ask me before retrying authentication.

output_examples.input: Inspect review feedback for my current branch.
output_examples.output: The assistant presents a numbered list of review threads, each with a short summary and the likely fix.

output: Comment 2 is fixed with a targeted code change.

output_examples.input: GitHub CLI auth fails during review triage.
output_examples.output: The assistant pauses, explains the authentication problem, and asks the user to re-authenticate before continuing.

best_practices: Review the numbered comment list before approving any edits.
Use the least GitHub access needed for the PR task.
Run tests or checks after selected fixes are applied.
anti_patterns: Do not grant broad GitHub scopes for simple comment reading.
Do not apply every review suggestion without user confirmation.
Do not rely on this skill when the GitHub CLI is unauthenticated.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on the GitHub CLI for authentication and PR comment access.

faq.question: Can it choose which comments to fix?
faq.answer: No. It should list comments and wait for the user to choose items.

faq.question: Does it include a comment fetching script?
faq.answer: No. The packaged file references fetch_comments.py, but only SKILL.md is present.

faq.question: Can it work without network access?
faq.answer: No. GitHub PR inspection requires network access to GitHub.

faq.question: Is it safe to grant workflow scope?
faq.answer: Grant workflow scope only when the task truly needs it. Most review comment work should use narrower access.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
